sentences.text: 1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The present petition has been filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeking quashing of the FIR No.296/2019 under Sections 419/420/468/471 IPC registered at Police Station Bindapur, Delhi on the ground that the parties have entered into a settlement.
4. Issue notice.
Learned APP for the State accepts notice.

He submits that since the present FIR has arisen out of a matrimonial dispute and the parties have entered into a settlement, the State has no objection, in case, the This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 16/09/2023 at 19:28:59 FIR is quashed.
5. The petitioner as well as, the respondent no.2 are present in Court and they have been identified by their respective counsels and by the Investigating Officer IO, SI Anup Rana, PS. Bindapur.
6. The brief facts of the case are that the marriage between the parties was solemnised on 29.10.2015 as per the Hindu Rites and Customs at Delhi.
No child was born out from the said wedlock.
Due to temperamental differences the parties started living separately w.e.f. 22.02.2018.

The dispute between the parties also led to the registration of another FIR being FIR No.221/2019 under Vanshika Singh @ Neetu Sharma vs State And Anr on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15791437/
1 Sections 498A/406/34 IPC.
7.

sentences.text:
During the pendency of the proceedings the parties have arrived at settlement dated 26.09.2022,
which is annexed as Annexure P-3 to the present petition.

8. On the basis of the said settlement the aforesaid cross FIR No.221/2019 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC has been quashed by this Court vide order dated 14.09.2023 passed in CRL.M.C.
6631/2023.
9.
It is also a term of the aforesaid settlement that the respondent No. 2 shall cooperate with the petitioner for the quashing of the present FIR.

10. Considering the fact that the present FIR is also an outcome of matrimonial dispute between the parties and they have already arrived at settlement, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
11. It is, thus, in the interest of justice that the present FIR and all the other proceedings emanating therefrom be quashed.
12. In view of the above, there is no legal impediment in quashing the present FIR in question.
Accordingly, FIR No.296/2019 under Sections This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 16/09/2023 at 19:28:59 419/420/468/471 IPC registered at Police Station Bindapur, Delhi is quashed along with all other consequential proceedings emanating there from.
13. The petition stands disposed off, in the above terms.
14. Order be uploaded on the website of this court.
VIKAS MAHAJAN, J SEPTEMBER 14, 2023 sc
